svg.title: Substitution models, spectral decay and SatuTe
svg.desc: Figure 1. Substitution models, spectral decay and SatuTe. a–c. Substitution models. The symbolic rate matrices use state order A, C, G, T. Each row sums to zero; μ normalizes the stationary mean substitution rate to one. In JC, α is the common rate before normalization. In K80, α and β are transition and transversion rates before normalization, with s = α + 2β. In GTR, (a, b, c, d, e, f) denote the symmetric exchangeabilities (r_AC, r_AG, r_AT, r_CG, r_CT, r_GT), and s_i = Σ_{j≠i} r_ij π_j. Illustrative parameter values. JC frequencies and eigenvalues are exact. K80 uses α/β = 3. GTR uses exchangeabilities (1, 4, 0.7, 1.2, 3, 0.8) in the order above and stationary frequencies (0.35, 0.15, 0.25, 0.25). The numerical K80 and GTR spectra and trajectories illustrate these choices; they are not fitted manuscript estimates. 3D probability space. Each tetrahedron is a 3D affine representation of four-state probability space. Probability vectors are columns: dp/dt = Qᵀp and Qᵀπ = 0. The nonstationary eigenvectors satisfy Qᵀvᵢ = λᵢvᵢ. The orange trajectory starts at p(0) = (1, 0, 0, 0)ᵀ. Circles mark t = 0.5, squares mark t = 2, and the black diamond marks the stationary distribution π as t → ∞. Time is measured in expected substitutions per site at stationarity. Dashed eigenvector directions are translated to π and scaled for display; they are not probability trajectories. Eigenvector signs and bases within repeated eigenspaces are arbitrary, while the probability trajectory is independent of that choice. JC has a multiplicity-three nonstationary eigenvalue; K80 here has multiplicities one and two. d–g. SatuTe. The manuscript uses h_i for left eigenvectors of Q. With the same eigenbasis and normalization, h_i = v_i: the probability directions above are the coherence directions below. They are normalized by h_iᵀ diag(π)⁻¹ h_j = δ_ij. (d) Alignment columns define site patterns. (e) Branch AB divides each site pattern into two subpatterns; their partial likelihoods give coherence coefficients. (f) Relative persistence weights compare each component with the slowest nonstationary component. SatuTe uses the weighted coherence to construct a z-score. The mode bars use the illustrated GTR model at t = 1; the relative weights are (1.000, 0.497, 0.242). (g) Rejection of subtree independence identifies phylogenetic signal.
